description: The projection / custom-property / Find delta, 108 lpn_ keys x 26 languages = 2,808 strings, run 2026-09-14 as one agent per language. Entries below are what the agents reported back, plus two collisions found by harvesting the shipped values afterwards and comparing them across languages -- a check no single agent could have run, because each sees only its own file.

entries.complaint: The shipped translations say "Open xy file on map" while the current English is "Open to new coordinates...". Independently hit by zh, de and ur in the same sprint, each reporting that the string in front of them did not describe the control. The English moved and the 26 translations did not.
readings: open an existing xy file onto a map (what the translations say)
open this project again under a different coordinate system (what the English says)
entries.resolution: Tom asked 2026-09-14: *"Should `en` be 'Convert coordinates as...'?"* **NO, and the code answers it twice.** (1) The row's own comment records that *"the old 'Convert to lat/lon...' row, which converted the OPEN project and had to be greyed whenever that project was already on the map, is gone with it"* -- so Convert names a command deliberately RETIRED, and restoring the name restores the confusion the removal bought. (2) Nothing is converted: `openAsGeoFile()` reads ANOTHER file and lands it in a NEW TAB as an upload, and a wizard places it on the world map by zoom, scale and rotate -- by eye, not by transform. 'Convert coordinates' would promise rewriting the user's numbers, which this suite refuses by rule (js/lpn-crs.js: *"converting rewrites every number somebody typed"*). **AND NEITHER OFFERED READING WAS RIGHT, INCLUDING TOM'S** -- it is not this project going to a new file, and not this project reopened; it is a DIFFERENT file arriving in a new tab. The finding framed the question wrongly, which is why every answer to it was wrong. **The shipped translations were closer to the behaviour than the current English**: 'Open xy file on map' names a file arriving on the map, which is what happens. So the English drifted away from the code and the translations did not. Proposed replacement put to Tom, not yet written: 'Open a file onto the world map...'.
entries.human_answer: The answer is 2 almost. The answer is "Open this project to a new file under a different coordinate system" (that is what the English says). Code has changed. Behavior has changed with the introduction of projections. Maybe _syn is needed: "Make a copy of a project file under a different coordinate system..." Should `en` be "Convert coordinates as..."?

entries.complaint: Duplicates lpn_cp_restrict word for word in English, so an agent translating both is asked to distinguish two strings that are identical. Caused the same day by the caption change that made restrictCaption() re-caption the character box from the mode's own option text.
entries.resolution: OPEN -- the two English values must differ or one key must go. Tom has not ruled. Raised in the handoff; it is cosmetic, not a wrong number, so it did not hold the sprint.

entries.complaint: "ALL CAPS" is prose sitting in a list whose other four members are code-convention NAMES (camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, hyphen-case) that must not be translated. Also reported by ar. Two agents resolved the tension by leaving it in English (ps, sr), which is the wrong half to keep: the other four are names of formats, this one is a description of one.
readings: the literal token ALL CAPS, a name like the four beside it
a description: every letter upper case
entries.resolution: FIXED. The four format names are now declared exempt globally in translation_exempt_keys.json -- identical to English is permanently correct there, because lpn_cp_bad_case quotes the format name back at the user and a translated one would name a rule the page does not apply. ALL CAPS is NOT exempt and was translated in ps and sr, the two that had left it.

entries.complaint: Northing/Easting and their one-letter abbreviations have no stable convention across languages, and the abbreviation keys assume the first letter of the word works. Answers ranged over Latin N/E, Turkish K/D, Ukrainian Pn/Sh, German Hochwert/Rechtswert (H/R) and Hebrew tsadi/mem. ARABIC CANNOT ABBREVIATE AT ALL: shamal and sharq both begin with the same letter, so a one-character abbreviation is ambiguous in a status bar that shows both at once.
readings: the coordinate axis of a projected grid
entries.resolution: Tom's ruling 2026-09-14: the abbreviation keys assume nothing, and the answer is a synonym rather than an English change -- _syn on the abbreviation key can carry the full word, and the abbreviation tag or the glossary can say it is an abbreviation OF that word. That is an INTENT case by the routing rule: an English reader does not stumble on 'N'; a translator cannot recover which N it is. The _syn diff is proposed to him for approval and is NOT yet written -- $ec_lang_syn takes explicit approval of the exact text, with no standing carve-out.
entries.human_answer: The abbreviation keys assume nothing. _syn Can say "Northing" and the abbreviation tag or glossary can say "Abbreviation of Northing". Use your judgement.

entries.complaint: FOUR LANGUAGES GIVE Tag AND THIS PAGE'S OWN Label THE IDENTICAL WORD: es Etiqueta, it Etichetta, sw Lebo, tr Etiket. lpn_field_tag and lpn_cp_label then stand in the same Properties box under one name. The synonym on lpn_field_tag says in as many words that it is not this page's Label object, so the guard was written and did not reach the outcome. Two of the four are anchor languages. Found by comparing the shipped values across all 26 files, which no single agent can do.
readings: EPANET's [TAGS] token, a grouping word the user chooses
the caption shown on a custom property
entries.resolution: CLOSED on Tom's ruling 2026-09-14, which DISMISSES the four-language collision rather than fixing it: *"Tag is just whatever ID-like synonym was available. The exact translation is not important because Tag has no real meaning."* He named Label and Custom label among its own synonyms, so es/it/sw/tr rendering Tag and Label with one word is sanctioned, not a defect. **The one live consequence, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug:** in those four languages the Properties box shows two adjacent fields under one name, and no rename is coming. A _syn carrying his synonym list is proposed to him and NOT yet written.
entries.human_answer: The truth is that "Tag" is just whatever ID-like synonym was available. The exact translation is not important because Tag has no real meaning. Maybe _syn could help ("Tag, Custom property, User property, Label, Custom label")

entries.complaint: THREE AGENTS MISSED THE SENSE OF "Projection": fa gave the psychological one, km a sorting system, sw a drawing. Nothing in the payload said which sense was meant, because there was no glossary term for it.
readings: map projection, which is the geometric sense applied to the globe
entries.resolution: FIXED at the mechanism. A new glossary term 'projection (map)' was created, harvested from the 23 renderings that took the right sense, and wired into prefixToTermNames()['lpn']. **Tom corrected the term's context the same day and the correction is the useful part:** *"Projection is in the geometric or optical sense also."* The first draft had ruled the optical sense OUT, which is backwards -- a map projection IS a geometric projection, the globe cast onto a plane, cone or cylinder, so a language reaching for its geometry word is correct. Only the psychological sense and 'a forecast' are the wrong ones. The three renderings are withheld from the term as UNCONFIRMED, not branded; their shipped strings are a resync, not this sprint's work.

entries.complaint: Composes as '{label}: {reason} The value is kept exactly as you typed it.' and every {reason} already ends in a full stop, so the two sentences run together with a single space and no break in some scripts.
entries.resolution: CLOSED on Tom's ruling 2026-09-14: the capital T makes the sentence start obvious to every translator, and no English change is needed. No further action.
entries.human_answer: The capital T makes a sentence start obvious to all translators. No ruling is needed.

entries.complaint: All 26 agents independently left camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case and hyphen-case untranslated, which lang_syntax_validate.php then blocked on as 104 identical-to-english findings. Unanimity across 26 languages is the definition of exempt, not of neglect.
readings: the name of a format the page checks against
entries.resolution: FIXED by declaration. The four keys are exempt with languages '*' in translation_exempt_keys.json. The underscore IS the snake_case convention, so the name cannot be carried into another script without naming a different rule than the one the page applies.
